title: The Recipe of Westbrook High
premise: Wren Underhill has survived Westbrook High by being forgettable—until an anonymous group chat called 'The Recipe' starts posting predictions that come true, and one of them names him. As the chat's prophecies grow darker and more personal, Wren realizes it's run by students who, like him, have been hiding who they are, and that its 'recipe' for survival is really a test of loyalty with a cruel price: expose someone else to stay safe yourself. When the final prediction targets the last game of the season and threatens to out his best friend, Wren chooses to break the recipe instead of follow it, unmasking the chat's creator—the quiet kid everyone overlooked—and claiming his own name in front of the whole town.
about_author: Rosalind Ravensworth grew up in a small mill town where everyone knew everyone's business except their own hearts. She writes stories about kids who learn that belonging shouldn't require disappearing.

chapters.title: Locker Shut
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. A routine Monday at Westbrook High establishes Wren's careful invisibility: perfect grades, no clubs, no parties, and a carefully neutral answer when a classmate asks if he's seeing anyone. The emotional beat is the exhaustion of constant self-editing, ending with him counting down 94 days to graduation.

chapters.title: Nine Hundred Witnesses
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. At Friday's football game, Wren watches from the bleachers as the town's whole social order performs itself. His childhood friend Delia drags him to the concession stand where he overhears seniors mocking 'the Underhill kid.' He laughs along to survive, then hates himself; the beat is complicity's bad taste.

chapters.title: The Invitation
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. A notification appears on his phone: he's been added to a group chat called 'The Recipe,' populated by seven anonymous handles. Its first message predicts a fire alarm for Tuesday, 10:14 a.m. Wren tells himself it's a prank. The beat is uneasy curiosity winning over caution.

chapters.title: Ten Fourteen
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Wren and Delia. The alarm rings at exactly 10:14. In the parking lot chaos, Wren locks eyes with another student—Marcus Vey—who looks as rattled by the timing as Wren feels. Delia notices Wren staring at his phone. The beat is the first crack in Wren's controlled world.

chapters.title: Ingredients
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The chat posts a second prediction: rain of paper from the second-floor window by Thursday. It comes true. Wren starts cataloguing the other members' writing styles, realizing they must all be students. The beat is detective-thriller momentum mixed with dread—he's inside something now.

chapters.title: Delia Knows Something
chapters.summary: Delia's POV. Delia confronts Wren about his distraction, and almost tells him her own secret—that she's been receiving messages too—but swerves into a fight about how he vanished from their friendship freshman year. The beat is two people hiding from each other in plain sight.

chapters.title: The First Name
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The chat posts its first prediction about a person: 'One of us stops coming to school after the dance.' When shy sophomore Priya Anand withdraws days later, Wren finds her crying behind the gym; she admits she was added to the chat weeks ago and told to recruit or be named. The beat is horror: the recipe requires ingredients.

chapters.title: Rules of the Kitchen
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The chat lays out its terms: each member must deliver a secret about someone else by month's end, or their own secret gets posted. Wren realizes the chat knows things about him it couldn't know unless someone close talked. The beat is paranoia tightening like a fist.

chapters.title: What Marcus Saw
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. Marcus Vey, the school's golden boy secretly struggling with his family's collapse, reveals he was the first recruit—targeted because the founder had leverage on him. He and Wren form a wary alliance, comparing clues. The beat is the relief and risk of letting someone in.

chapters.title: Homecoming, Interrupted
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. At homecoming, the chat executes a public prediction: the principal's resignation letter read over the speakers. In the panic, someone slips a note into Wren's pocket: 'You're next. Bring a secret or bring a name.' The beat is terror wearing a party dress.

chapters.title: The Price List
chapters.summary: Delia's POV. Delia discovers she's been drafted as leverage—her secret (an abortion last summer) is in the founder's files. She decides to tell Wren everything before the chat can use her against him. The beat is courage arriving late but arriving.

chapters.title: Confessions at the Diner
chapters.summary: Wren and Delia dual POV. Over fries at the Blue Plate, both come clean: Delia's secret, Wren's sexuality, and the years of distance between them. They agree to find the founder together. The beat is grief and gratitude tangled—belonging rebuilt from honesty.

chapters.title: Suspects
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren and Marcus narrow candidates using writing-style analysis and access patterns: the chat always posts during fourth period. Suspicion falls on three students, including quiet yearbook editor Theo Brandt. The beat is the moral discomfort of doing to others what the chat does to them.

chapters.title: Wrong Turn
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Acting on a planted clue, Wren publicly accuses the wrong student, who is viciously bullied as a result. The chat posts a single message: 'See how easy? You're learning the recipe.' The beat is Wren confronting that he's becoming the thing he fears.

chapters.title: Priya Comes Back
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya returns to school changed—angrier, braver—and joins the alliance, revealing the founder's original recruitment message contained a detail about the old Underhill house that only a longtime local would know. The beat is the hunted becoming hunters.

chapters.title: Inheritance
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Digging through his late grandmother's things, Wren finds letters suggesting the 'Recipe' began decades ago as a student survival network for kids like him—a chain of secrets passed down that curdled into blackmail under this year's keeper. The beat is inheritance as both wound and inheritance as gift.

chapters.title: The Keeper
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo Brandt is revealed as this year's keeper: he inherited the chat from his older brother and convinced himself the cruelty was protection. Cornered by Wren, Theo argues that exposure destroys people here—look what happened to his brother. The beat is a villain who is also a warning.

chapters.title: The Last Prediction
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Theo refuses to end the chat without a successor, and posts the final prediction: 'Before the last whistle Friday night, one of you will be named to the whole town.' The countdown begins. Wren realizes the target is Delia—and that refusing means naming himself instead. The beat is the trap closing.

chapters.title: Ninety-Four Days, Spent
chapters.summary: Dual POV, Wren and Delia. The alliance fractures under pressure: Marcus wants to feed Theo a stranger's secret to buy safety; Priya wants to go to the administration; Delia says she'll out herself first so no one else pays. Wren must choose whose survival matters. The beat is love tested against self-preservation.

chapters.title: Last Game
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Under the Friday-night lights, with nine hundred townspeople watching, the chat goes live on every phone in the stadium. Before Theo's message can name Delia, Wren climbs the fence, takes the megaphone, and speaks his own truth first—naming himself, naming the recipe, naming Theo. The beat is terror transfigured into freedom.

chapters.title: After the Whistle
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Fallout: Theo faces consequences but also, unexpectedly, the beginning of help; Marcus owns his part publicly; the town reckons with what it made its kids do to survive. Wren and Delia walk the empty field afterward. The beat is the fragile, unglamorous morning after courage.

chapters.title: A New Recipe
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, epilogue. Graduation day. Wren, Delia, Priya, and Marcus start a small, honest version of the old network—an open letter circle, no secrets required. Wren adds his grandmother's letters to the first entry. The beat is belonging chosen freely, inheritance redeemed, and the price of survival finally paid in full.
